A variable listed by name.
A family listed by name.
A list with one name.
Lists read "x and y", "x, y and z".
A variable used as a term.
The last claim of a conclusion.
natural number, ℕ.
finite set of … is Finset, not Set.
A bijection is an Equiv, which carries its inverse.
∈ as membership.
∉ as non-membership.
⊆ as inclusion; a finite set on the left is coerced to a set.
⊈ as the negation of ⊆.
∖ as set difference; a finite set on the right is coerced.
L_i is the i-th language of the family introduced with letter L.
|S| ≥ n means n ≤ card S.
has length at least n means n ≤ length.
p is a prefix of w is List.IsPrefix p w.
the set of values of f is exactly X is range f = X: every value lies in X and every element of X occurs.
every value of f lies in X is range f ⊆ X.
Injective.
and is ∧; a compound left conjunct is bracketed.
{i ∈ X : P} for a finite X is a finite set (Finset.filter).
Let x ∈ ℕ. / "Let x be a T." binds x for the rest of the text.
Let x be a T with P. binds x and assumes P for the rest of the text.
Let x ∈ X. binds x with x ∈ X assumed.
As LetIn, with one further assumption.
Let t ≥ T. binds a natural number t with T ≤ t assumed.
Assume that equality on A is decidable. is an instance argument, not a hypothesis about A.
Let x be … or "Let x = …" is a local definition, not an assumption.
Let o(t) be … defines a sequence; t is a dummy.
Call a T adj if it … defines a property; later "x is adj" means exactly that property.
x is adj applies a property defined earlier in the text.
Suppose that P. assumes P for the rest of the text. The proof of P has no name; a later term may use it through `by assumption`.
There is x ∈ ℕ, depending only on …, with the following property. The rest of the text is the property. The dependency list is checked at elaboration (depends_only%), not by the kernel.
Then … states the conclusion.
P. Also, Q. is P ∧ Q.
P for every x ∈ X covers only P; "for every x ∈ X, P" covers all of P.
for every t ≥ T, P inside a claim; t is a natural number.
P for every x ∈ ℕ covers only the atomic claim P.
for all natural numbers x, y and z, P.
there is … such that P.
Then A is infinite. also supplies the proof that the next sentence uses.
Let u list the elements of A in increasing order. is IRStatement.increasingEnumeration: least element, then least element above the previous one. Review that definition once.
{x(n) : n < t} is GenLimit.sample for ℕ-valued x and GenLimit.Generic.sample otherwise (IRStatement.FirstTerms).

An indexed family of languages L_0, L_1, … Each L_i is infinite. O has a membership oracle. is GenLimit.OracleFamily or IndexedOracleFamily: languages, infinitude, a Boolean query and its correctness.
⊆ ℕ selects GenLimit.OracleFamily.
of words over A selects IndexedOracleFamily (List A).
the oracle confirms x ∈ L_i is O.query i x = true, not x ∈ L_i itself.
the membership-query generator for O is GenLimit.OracleFamily.kmGenerator O, the paper's Section 5 algorithm.
the prompted membership-query generator for O with coding e is GenLimit.KM.Prompted.generatorOfEquiv e O, the Appendix A.5 algorithm.
the output of G on x at step t is G x t: the output after the first t observations.
the output of G on x and p at step t is G x p h t, where h is the robustness hypothesis found by `by assumption`.
has arbitrarily long extensions in every L_i means: for all i and n, some word c with length at least n has subject · c ∈ L_i.
A list with one item.
Items of a bullet list, joined by ∧.
One type argument.
Type arguments, listed in Lean's order.
One argument.
Arguments, comma-separated in Lean's order.
An oracle family used as a term.
A numeral.
ℝ.
ℤ.
Bool, the Booleans.
Prop.
A bound type variable α; an element of it is described in words: “an element x of α”.
Set T; over ℕ or a type variable α it is a subset: “S ⊆ α”.
List T; over a type variable A it is a word: “a word over A”.
Option T: an element of T or none.
A function type A → B: “a function from A to B”. A domain or codomain that is a list, set or finite set is named in words (“lists of natural numbers”), and a product as A × B.
A × B.
A ⊕ B.
An injective function packaged as A ↪ B.
A type constant: “a *label*”.
A type constant with type arguments: “a *label* over A and B”.
A constant with no explicit argument: “*label*”.
A function constant: “*label*(X₁, …, Xₖ)”, arguments in Lean's order.
A predicate constant with one argument: “X is *label*”, or “X *label*” when the label begins with a verb (has, is, can, …).
Its negation: “X is not *label*”, or “it is false that X *label*” for a verb label.
A predicate constant with several arguments: “*label*(X₁, …, Xₖ)”.
Its negation: “*label*(X₁, …, Xₖ) does not hold”; no quantifier follows it.
A proposition constant: “*label* holds”.
An instance argument for a class constant: “Assume that α is *label*”.
f(X₁, …, Xₖ) applies a variable to arguments.
P(X₁, …, Xₖ) applies a predicate variable.
Its negation: “P(X₁, …, Xₖ) does not hold”; no quantifier follows it.
A propositional variable used as a claim.
− is truncated subtraction on ℕ.
· is multiplication.
/ is Lean's division of the type at hand.
Negation.
↑X is the cast of X to the type required by its context.
(x ↦ X) is a function; the type of x is the one its context requires.
“the property x ↦ P” is a predicate; the type of x is the one its context requires.
{x ∈ T : P} is the set of x in the type T with P.
{x ∈ T ∖ S : P} is {x | x ∉ S ∧ P}.
“Suppose that P, and call this assumption h.” binds a proof h of P that later terms use.

“There is x … with the following property.” with no dependency list. Used when nothing has been introduced before, or when the property introduces no variable of its own, so the choice can depend on everything above.
A claim stated on its own, with nothing assumed in this text before it.
“All of the following hold:” then a bullet per claim; the claims are joined by ∧.
“The following are equivalent:” then two bullets: the first ↔ the second.
“At least one of the following holds:” then two bullets: the first ∨ the second.
“Exactly one of the following holds:” is (P ∧ ¬Q) ∨ (¬P ∧ Q).
“or” is inclusive; a different connective on the right is bracketed.
“if and only if”; compound sides are bracketed.
“if P, then Q”.
“it is not the case that P”; its scope is the rest of the claim.
“there is no … such that P” is ¬∃.
“there is x ∈ X such that P” is ∃ x ∈ X, P.
“there is x ≥ y such that P” is ∃ x ≥ y, P, with x a natural number.
“for infinitely many n ∈ ℕ” is ∃ᶠ n in atTop.
“for all sufficiently large n ∈ ℕ” is ∀ᶠ n in atTop.
A sequence is a function on ℕ; its symbol is T^ℕ.
“a type” is Type u for some universe u.
“a type in the lowest universe” is Type 0.
“a sort” is Sort u: a type or a universe of propositions.
(L_i) is the whole family O.language, as a function of the index.
“P; call this fact h.” asserts P and names its proof h for later terms (∃ h : P, …).
An oracle family O as the argument of a type constructor.
(L_i), the languages of O, as the argument of a type constructor.
“Let x, y and z be Ts.” binds several variables of one type. For “Let A and B be types.” Lean gives each binder its own universe.
“There are x ∈ T and y ∈ U, depending only on …, with the following property.” chooses several objects at once; the dependency list is checked at elaboration.
As ThereAre, with no dependency list, under the same conditions as ThereIsFree.
One chosen object.
Chosen objects, listed in Lean's order.
(X, Y) is the ordered pair of X and Y.
() is the only element of the type with one element.
[] is the empty list.
[X₁, …, Xₖ] is the list of X₁, …, Xₖ in this order.
⟨X⟩ is X as an element of a subtype, such as C(z) as an element of the range of C. The membership proof is left to Lean; by proof irrelevance any proof gives the same term.
“Let F = …, with languages M_0, M_1, M_2, ….” names a family of languages given by a formula; M_i is its i-th language. A local definition, not an assumption.
“Assume that *label*(A, B).” is an instance argument [c A B] of a class with several arguments.
“an element of L(i)”: the type given by applying a variable L to arguments.
{0, …, k − 1} is Fin k, the natural numbers below k.
{0, …, m} with a numeral m is Fin (m + 1).
(x ∈ T ↦ Y) is the function fun (x : T) => Y; used when Y does not mention x, so the type cannot be inferred.
“By definition, P if and only if Q.” is P ↔ Q. In the glossary, P is a label applied to its parameters; “by definition” holds because the statement is proved by Iff.rfl (Glossary.lean).
“By definition, P if and only if the following holds.” followed by the rest of the text is P ↔ (the rest).
“By definition, X = Y.” is X = Y; in the glossary, proved by rfl.
“By definition, a T is a U.” is the equation T = U of types; in the glossary, proved by rfl.
“an element of *label*(1)”: a type constant applied to a number, such as Lattice 1.
“the set F” is the finite set F as a set (Finset.toSet F, Lean's coercion).
“an element of *label*(d + 2)”: a type constant applied to a variable plus a number, such as Lattice (d + 2).
“a member x of S” is x : ↥S, an element of the set S as a type ({x // x ∈ S}).
“P for every i < n” (atomic P) or “for every i < n, P” is ∀ i : ℕ, i < n → P.
“there is i < n such that P” is ∃ i : ℕ, i < n ∧ P.
